title: Shading a fraction of a grid: parts of the whole, not the top number
familyTitle: How many squares to shade to show a fraction
skill: Shade a/b of a grid of n equal squares: n ÷ b squares per part, a parts.

concept: A fraction names equal parts of ONE whole. The bottom number is how many equal parts the whole is cut into, all of them, shaded or not.
The top number is how many of those parts we mean. So the fraction of a shape that is shaded is (shaded parts) over (all the equal parts).
explanation.visualNote: Reuses the family's own empty grid figure.

workedExamples.prompt: The grid in the picture has 15 equal squares. How many squares must be shaded to show 2/5 of the grid?
lines: Share 15 squares into 5 equal parts: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 squares in each part
2 parts: 2 × 3 = 6 squares

hints: Into how many equal parts must the grid be shared for /5?
How many squares are in each part?

alternativeExplanation.title: Two wholes
text: Half of a small grid and half of a big grid are different numbers of squares, but each is half of its own grid.

whatWentWrong: In "The grid in the picture has 18 equal squares. How many squares must be shaded to show 7/9 of the grid?", one wrong answer is 7.
7 squares were shaded, the top number. The top number counts parts of size 1/9 of the WHOLE grid, and each such part here is 2 squares.
The top number counts PARTS of the whole, and each part may be several squares.
screens.counterCheck: Check: 7 squares out of 18 is 7/18, not 7/9.
solvedCorrectly: Share 18 squares into 9 equal parts: 18 ÷ 9 = 2 squares in each part
